samples.summary: Frontend-wide URL rule + new `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts` primitive is documented only in the CLI design doc; the canonical frontend subsystem doc is untouched
samples.evidence: The change introduces a new shared frontend primitive (`packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts`) and applies it across every browser API module (documents, workspaces, folders, share-links, datasources, files, analytics, miro, spreadsheet image upload). The only design-doc record of this is a paragraph inside `docs/design/cli.md` §10 ("The rule is not CLI-only… `seg()`, `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts`… applied to **every** browser API module"). `docs/design/frontend.md` — the canonical doc for the browser client, which already documents the API layer and `fetchWithAuth` 401 handling at lines ~412-445 — contains no mention of `seg`, `url.ts`, or the path-segment rule (grep for `seg\(|url.ts|path segment` in docs/design/frontend.md: no matches). CONTRIBUTING/design discipline expects an architecture rule to be folded into the canonical subsystem doc rather than described from a neighbouring package's doc; as written, a future frontend contributor reading frontend.md has no way to learn that every route-param id must go through `seg()`. Also note the top-level backtick-path check does not validate that cli.md's frontend claims stay true as frontend modules are added.
searchedFor: read the diff for any docs/design/frontend.md hunk (none present)

samples.summary: `seg()` is implemented twice (CLI and frontend) instead of extracted to the shared package the repo uses for exactly this
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/client/url.ts` and `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts` are byte-for-byte the same function (dot-segment refusal + `encodeURIComponent`) with parallel doc comments that each point at the other. `docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md` sets the bar as "Tier C/D stay out until a concrete second consumer exists" (lines 239-241) — this change *creates* the second consumer, and the frontend already depends on `@wafflebase/core` (packages/frontend/package.json:57). The CLI does not depend on core today, so extraction has a real cost; hence minor rather than major, but the duplicated invariant (and its duplicated error string, which the tests in both packages assert on) will drift.

samples.summary: New `WAFFLEBASE_IMAGE_HOSTS` knob is read straight from `process.env` in a leaf module, bypassing the CLI's single config-resolution layer
samples.evidence: Every other CLI knob is resolved in `packages/cli/src/config/config.ts` with the documented precedence flags > env > session > config profile (`resolveConfig`, lines 77-167), and surfaces on `CliConfig`. `createImageFetcher` instead does `process.env[IMAGE_HOSTS_ENV]` at call time, so the new setting has no `--image-hosts` flag and no `profiles.<name>` config-file key, and cannot be seen by `wafflebase status`/`ctx`. That is a layer mismatch with §3 of docs/design/cli.md for a knob an operator of a self-hosted install is expected to set persistently.

samples.summary: `assertNoDotSegments` re-implements `seg()`'s dot-segment refusal instead of reusing it, so the same invariant now lives in three places
samples.evidence: `printDryRun` splits the path and throws the same `Invalid path segment: "…"` message that `seg()` (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:24) throws, purely as a backstop for a call site that forgot to encode. A cleaner fit would be for `printDryRun` to take already-segmented pieces (or a small path builder) rather than a pre-joined string it then re-parses; as written the message string is duplicated a third time (CLI seg, frontend seg, dry-run assert) and the query-string carve-out is bespoke parsing in a printer.
searchedFor: read packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts and url.ts in the diff
grep 'Invalid path segment' across the diff

samples.summary: Four independent concerns are bundled into one change, making the design intent hard to evaluate or revert piecemeal
samples.evidence: The diff couples (1) one-segment id encoding in CLI + frontend, (2) a full rewrite of upstream-error classification (`forwardUpstreamError`/`upstreamErrorJson`/`UpstreamHttpError`, plus moving api-keys onto `requestUrl`), (3) an SSRF guard for the export image fetcher with a new env var and manual redirect following, and (4) a changed `files download` filename fallback (`docId` → `basename`/`download`). Each is a separate behavioural contract with its own design-doc paragraph in cli.md §10. No originating issue was supplied with this review, so I cannot check them against a stated outcome/acceptance list; flagging the breadth so the author can confirm all four were in scope.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts` is a real new frontend-wide primitive (`seg()`), used in 19 frontend files spanning documents, workspaces, folders, share-links, datasources, files, analytics, miro and the spreadsheet image upload. Its only design-doc record is docs/design/cli.md:1147-1157. I searched every `*.md` in the repo for `seg\(|url\.ts|path segment` (and `encodeURIComponent` across docs/): the only design-doc hit is cli.md; everything else is docs/tasks execution plans or agent-review scratch. docs/design/frontend.md — indexed as the canonical browser-client doc at docs/design/README.md:152 and already documenting the API layer and fetchWithAuth 401 handling at :412-445 — has no mention of the rule. CONTRIBUTING.md:57-61 requires updating the existing doc for the area being evolved, so the frontend area's architecture rule living only in a neighbouring package's doc is a design-doc-discipline miss in this lens's lane. No counterexample found anywhere; the only mitigation is the source-file docblock in url.ts:1-17, which is code, not a design doc.
